title: Richter's Bounded Maximum Degree Conjecture
statement_text: For every positive integer $c$, there exists an integer $D(c)$ such that every $c$-crossing-critical graph has maximum degree fewer than $D(c)$.
context_text: Richter conjectured in 2003 that the maximum degree in $c$-crossing-critical graphs is bounded by a function of $c$ alone. The conjecture was disproved non-constructively by Dvořák and Mohar for $c \geq 171$ in 2010. The paper resolves the conjecture completely by showing it holds exactly for $c \leq 12$ and fails for all $c \geq 13$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture holds for every $c \leq 12$ (Theorem 1.1) and disproves it for every $c \geq 13$ via explicit constructions of 3-connected $c$-crossing-critical graphs containing arbitrarily many vertices of arbitrarily large degree (Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3).
paper_title: Bounded maximum degree conjecture holds precisely for $c$-crossing-critical graphs with $c \leq 12$

title: Optimal degree bounds $D_c$ for small $c$
statement_text: Determine the optimal values of $D_c$ for each $c \in \{2, 3, \ldots, 12\}$, where $D_c$ is the smallest integer such that every $c$-crossing-critical graph has maximum degree at most $D_c$.
context_text: Graphs are multigraphs by default (parallel edges allowed). The crossing number $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ is the minimum number of crossings in a drawing of $G$ in the plane. For a positive integer $c$, a graph is $c$-crossing-critical if $\operatorname{cr}(G)\ge c$ but every proper subgraph has crossing number less than $c$. Richter conjectured in 2003 that for every $c$ the maximum degree of $c$-crossing-critical graphs is bounded; Dvořák and Mohar disproved this for every $c\ge171$, non-constructively. The authors settle the question for all $c$: using Hliněný's bounded path-width result and the structural classification of large $c$-crossing-critical graphs by Dvořák, Hliněný and Mohar, they prove that there is an integer $D$ such that every $c$-crossing-critical graph with $c\le12$ has maximum degree at most $D$, while for every $c\ge13$ they construct 3-connected $c$-crossing-critical graphs with arbitrarily many vertices of arbitrarily large degree. Thus finite optimal bounds $D_c$ exist for $c\le 12$, but the proof is asymptotic and gives no explicit values. Known: $D_1=4$ (1-crossing-critical graphs are the subdivisions of $K_5$ and $K_{3,3}$), $D_2\ge8$, and the optimal $D_2$ should be within reach using the characterization of 2-crossing-critical graphs by Bokal, Oporowski, Richter and Salazar; the remaining values are left to future investigations (the authors list this among their final open problems, for each $c\le12$).
notes: Stated as a future-work direction rather than a formally labelled open problem; Section 7 (open problems) was not included in the provided text excerpt.
paper_title: Bounded maximum degree conjecture holds precisely for $c$-crossing-critical graphs with $c \leq 12$
